title: Scalar tests when the whole boundary cosphere is allowed
reviewed_arguments: H0 retains compact nonempty boundary and the full allowed boundary-cosphere hypothesis; the entire bounded family, uniform residual tails, original Banach norm and exact parameter quantifiers remain.
C0 obtains one full-fiber collar from compactness and fixes all exact normal support buffers. The cylinder proofs apply on their smooth Schwartz domain; no larger graph-density claim is made.

H1 constructs actual global spanning fields and their fixed-density adjoints. H2 proves the exact positive quadratic form and all differential-power coercivity without a spectral theorem or a claimed boundary inverse.

H3 gives the complete finite-chart frozen-principal Fourier estimate, leading-coefficient absorption, lower-order commutators and finite Fourier interpolation with constants chosen in the correct order.

L0 computes the full logarithmic phase and positive frequency Jacobian with the exact density ratio. Translated compact v-windows, uniform derivative bounds and finite overlap use the actual compact amplitude theorem.
L0 retains every full rectangular and cross-component log tail with both Schur integrals. L1 uses exact right Fourier multiplication and the actual packet bound for the whole collar family.
The far collar output is genuinely diagonal-separated and flat in the input. It is not an untested full boundary residual assigned to the Banach-only remainder.
A0 computes both smooth unitary conjugations, including all half powers, and gives an actual compact scalar b-differential collar test with the exact physical norm.

A1 constructs the positive interior addition with both complete projections away from the deep cutoff. The full collar/interior ellipticity overlap covers the entire transition, including outer cutoff derivatives.

A2 checks every full EA input projection: the collar test is differential on the diagonal and the interior addition has interior input. Every remaining proper, low-frequency and far error is therefore original smooth with flat input.
T0 recovers the whole collar norm from one scalar A and the original Banach term, then applies the exact three-term split of every target operator.
All three solutions check the exact circular three-quarter gauge, the full buffer interval and the inverse-kernel jump, multiplier and both nonflat ratio powers.
Compact fully base-covered boundaries with restricted allowed angular directions and the full general observation graph remain open.

The current component scope paragraphs were visually inspected at desktop and mobile widths. All formulas parse, display and figure extents are accessible, and the component retains its stated hypotheses and actual tested-graph scope.
